newsitem.title: USA: Beef, pork exports to Bulgaria seen rising - attache.
newsitem.headline: Beef, pork exports to Bulgaria seen rising - attache.

text.p: Bulgaria will be a good market for U.S. exporters of beef and pork in 1997 and 1998 because of the government's trade liberalization, according to an agricultural attache report made public on Wednesday.
The report, prepared by the U.S. embassy in Sofia, said Bulgaria would increase imports of beef, pork, tallow, hides and skin because of an expected decline in production and trade liberalization.

In 1997, the Bulgarian government has forecast pork imports of 35,000 tonnes and beef imports of 15,000 tonnes. Imports will rise in 1998 to 40,000 tonnes and 25,000 tonnes, respectively, the report said.

"However, a key factor which is preventing the U.S. from expanding in this potentially large beef market (US$23 million in 1995) is Bulgaria's veterinary requirement which does not allow imports of beef with hormones," the report said.
The report said traders were looking for U.S. frozen unboned beef and pork in halves, offal, and hides and skins.

Despite Bulgaria's restrictions on importing beef with hormones the United States had an eight percent market share of total beef imports last year, the report said. The U.S. share of pork imports was 23 percent because of favorable U.S. prices.
